notes:
User enjoys healthy, reheatable meals and meal prep. They recently bought a new Instant Pot and Air Fryer. They made Korean Chicken Stew (Jjimdak) using bite-size chicken breast, reduced high-pressure cooking to about 10–12 minutes, targeting 165°F/74°C internal temperature; breast may be dry, and gochugaru was reduced to 1 Tbsp to limit heat. Suggested gochugaru brands: Sempio or Koko.

For this week’s meal, they considered bean/lentil dishes similar to chili and plan to make a Cuban black bean and rice bowl with onion, bell pepper, garlic, brown rice, avocado, and lime. They chose easy fruit salad as dessert (strawberries, grapes, kiwi, pineapple, lime, optional mint; lightly sweeten if desired).

They plan crispy Air Fryer sweet potato fries: use uniform thin cuts, soak in cold water, dry thoroughly, lightly oil, air-fry at 400°F/200°C around 12–15 minutes in batches, shake halfway, and season after cooking.

For bowl leftovers, refrigerate promptly in shallow airtight containers for 3–4 days or freeze portions for longer; reheat rice/beans/vegetables to 165°F/74°C. Fries will soften in storage; for longer storage, freeze separately, then re-crisp in Air Fryer/oven. Avoid leavin
trajectory: User is meal-prepping healthy, reheatable lunches and recently bought a new Instant Pot. They are making Korean Chicken Stew (Jjimdak) and plan to use chicken breast rather than thighs/drumsticks, cut into bite-size pieces, with pressure-cooking time reduced to about 10–12 minutes at high pressure; internal temperature should reach 165°F/74°C. Chicken breast may be drier, so it may be worth combining it with thighs. They chose to reduce gochugaru (Korean chili flakes) from 2 Tbsp to 1 Tbsp because they are new to gochujang and concerned about heat; they can season to taste afterward. Base recipe discussed: sesame oil; chicken; onion, garlic, potatoes, carrots; 2 Tbsp gochujang, 2 Tbsp soy sauce, 2 Tbsp brown sugar, black pepper, chicken broth, optional green onions. Suggested brands: Sempio or Koko gochugaru; Sunchang or Chongga gochujang. User is currently preparing ingredients and appreciates guidance on spice level and chicken breast timing.
